subtopics.name: How Communication Takes Place in Business

parts.problem_md: Define the term **internal communication**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - The exchange of information between people within the same business **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - The sharing of messages/information between employees or departments inside a business **[1 mark]**
> 
> "Define" requires a clear, precise statement of the meaning of the term

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you emphasise that the communication takes place *within* the business. A common mistake is to give a general definition of communication without specifying that it is internal — i.e. between people in the same organisation. Avoid confusing internal communication with external communication, which involves parties outside the business.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Most people recognise Heinz for the phrase ‘57 varieties’ even though it now produces many more than the original 57 varieties. H J Heinz, the founder of the Heinz business, believed the phrase sounded lucky.
> 
> *Kraft Heinz* is a world-wide producer of food products. It was formed from the merger of Kraft Foods and Heinz in 2015. This created the third largest food and drinks business in the USA and the fifth largest food and drinks business in the world.
> 
> *Kraft Heinz* has over 24 different brands, including Greenseas in Australia and Nutri+Plus in New Zealand. America has the largest number of brands from Maxwell House to Cool Whip.* Kraft Heinz *produces many different products including tomato sauce, ‘Mac&Cheese’, pasta and its famous baked beans that are used and eaten by many people.
> 
> *Kraft Heinz* uses many methods to advertise its products. These include posters, billboards and leaflets in supermarkets.

Which **one** of the following is an example of external communication?

Select **one **answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B**

Sending a customer details of a special offer is an external communication because it involves communicating with a party outside the organisation.

**A** is incorrect as a presentation by the chairperson to employees is an internal communication

**C** is incorrect as a departmental meeting is an internal communication

**D** is incorrect as training sessions for new employees is an internal communication

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: A presentation by the chairperson to its employees

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Sending a customer details of a special offer

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Premier Inn has over 820 hotels in the UK, United Arab Emirates (UAE), India and Germany with over 83,000 rooms. The majority of the hotels have restaurants with facilities for guests to buy meals and drinks. Premier Inn wants to retain its employees so it can continue to maintain the service it provides for guests.

State one method of communication Premier Inn could use to share information with its employees across different countries.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any 1 from:
> 
> - Email / video conferencing to send information to employees in its hotels across the UK, UAE, India and Germany
> - A company intranet that allows staff across all 820 hotels to access important updates and documents
> - Newsletters / notice boards within each hotel to inform staff about changes to procedures or company news
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a method of communication that is not in the context of Premier Inn
> 
> "State" requires the student to provide a clear, brief answer without further explanation

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you relate your answer to the context of Premier Inn operating across multiple countries. A generic method of communication without any link to the business is unlikely to earn the mark. Think about what would be practical for a large, international hotel chain — for example, email or a company intranet — rather than methods that would only work within a single location.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> BrightWave Electronics is a growing technology company based in Manchester. It designs and manufactures smart home devices, selling them to customers across the UK and Europe. The company employs over 200 staff across its head office, warehouse and two retail stores.
> 
> BrightWave recently launched a new product range and used a variety of methods to promote it. These included email newsletters to existing customers, social media advertisements and in-store displays. Internally, the company held team briefings and updated its staff intranet to keep employees informed about the launch.

Which **one** of the following is an example of internal communication?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is D**

A staff briefing about new company procedures is an internal communication because it involves communicating with people within the organisation.

**A** is incorrect as sending a press release to a newspaper is an external communication

**B** is incorrect as emailing a supplier about a delivery is an external communication

**C** is incorrect as posting an advertisement on social media is an external communication

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Sending a press release to a newspaper

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Emailing a supplier about a delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Posting an advertisement on social media

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: A staff briefing about new company procedures

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Kraft Heinz is a world-wide producer of food products with factories in over 29 countries. It has over 24 different brands, including Greenseas in Australia and Maxwell House in America.

Outline one problem Kraft Heinz may face from ineffective communication
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a valid problem and a further 1 mark for development of the problem.
> 
> Any pair from (1 mark per point):
> 
> - If communication between Kraft Heinz's factories in 29 different countries is ineffective, production errors could occur **[1 mark]**
> - This could lead to products such as baked beans or pasta being made to the wrong specification, resulting in waste and increased costs **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Ineffective communication could mean that important health and safety information is not shared properly across Kraft Heinz's global operations **[1 mark]**
> - This could put employees at risk and lead to legal action or fines, damaging the reputation of its 24 brands **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - If marketing messages are not communicated clearly between countries, Kraft Heinz could promote the wrong products in the wrong markets **[1 mark]**
> - For example, advertising Greenseas in America instead of Australia would waste money and fail to reach the intended customers **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> "Outline" requires a brief statement of the key point (1 mark) with some development or context (1 mark).

> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked to "outline", make sure you do two things: identify the problem clearly and then develop it with a brief explanation or example. A common mistake is to simply name a problem without linking it back to the business in the extract. Use the information given — for instance, referring to Kraft Heinz's global operations across 29 countries or its 24 brands — to make your answer specific and contextual. Avoid listing multiple problems; focus on one and develop it well to secure both marks.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Define the term **external communication**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - The exchange of information/messages between a business and people or organisations outside of it **[1 mark]**
> 
> Alternative acceptable answers include:
> 
> - The sharing of messages or information between a business and its customers, suppliers or other outside parties
> 
> "Define" requires a clear, precise statement of the meaning of the term.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your definition includes two key elements: the idea of information being exchanged, and the fact that it involves parties **outside** the business. A common mistake is to give a definition that could equally apply to internal communication — always specify that the communication is with external individuals or organisations such as customers, suppliers or the government.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> GreenLeaf Logistics is a medium-sized delivery company based in Birmingham. It operates a fleet of 150 vehicles and employs around 300 staff, including warehouse workers, drivers and office-based managers.
> 
> The company recently introduced a new scheduling system for its drivers. However, many drivers reported that they did not fully understand the instructions because the technical language used in the training manual was too complex. Some drivers who speak English as a second language found it particularly difficult. Managers also noticed that important messages sent by email were often missed by warehouse staff who do not regularly access computers during their shifts.

Which **one** of the following is an example of a barrier to communication?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B**

Using technical jargon that employees do not understand is a barrier to communication because it prevents the message from being received and understood clearly by the intended audience.

**A** is incorrect as holding a face-to-face meeting with staff is a method of communication, not a barrier

**C** is incorrect as sending a written memo to all departments is a method of communication, not a barrier

**D** is incorrect as providing training sessions for new employees is a way of improving communication, not a barrier

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Holding a face-to-face meeting with staff

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Using technical jargon that employees do not understand

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Sending a written memo to all departments

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Providing training sessions for new employees

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> LEGO is a privately-owned business in Denmark. It is one of the world's largest manufacturers of toys, with 15 factories and over 18,000 employees around the world. LEGO manufactures toys, games and art materials for boys and girls of all ages, and products from films such as Star Wars and Harry Potter.

State one reason why effective communication is important for LEGO
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any 1 from:
> 
> - To ensure that all 15 factories around the world are producing products to the same quality standards
> - To make sure its 18,000 employees across different countries understand any changes to product designs or new product launches such as Star Wars or Harry Potter ranges
> - To coordinate production and delivery across its global operations so that products reach customers on time
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> "State" requires the student to provide a clear, brief point without the need for further explanation or justification.
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a reason that is not in the context of LEGO

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you apply your answer to the context of LEGO rather than giving a generic reason. Use details from the extract, such as the number of factories, employees or product ranges, to show the examiner you understand why communication matters specifically for this business. A common mistake is to give a vague answer like "so people know what to do" — instead, link your reason to a specific feature of LEGO's operations mentioned in the extract.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Saving the environment in which we all live is important. The Chairman ensures that Emirates works hard to recycle many of the materials it uses and to reduce atmospheric pollution from the fuel that powers its aircraft. Emirates uses a variety of methods to monitor its employees when carrying out these jobs. For these roles Emirates uses a short chain of command.

Outline one benefit to Emirates of using a short chain of command for communication.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a valid benefit. Award a further 1 mark for development of the benefit.
> 
> - Messages reach employees more quickly because there are fewer levels for information to pass through **[1 mark]**
> - This means Emirates staff carrying out recycling and pollution reduction tasks receive instructions faster, reducing the chance of mistakes or delays **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - A short chain of command means communication is less likely to be distorted or misunderstood **[1 mark]**
> - This helps Emirates to ensure that its environmental procedures, such as recycling materials and reducing water consumption, are followed correctly by all employees **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - With fewer levels of management, employees can give feedback directly to senior staff **[1 mark]**
> - This allows Emirates to quickly identify and solve any problems with its environmental practices, such as issues with recycling newspapers collected from aircraft cabins **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> "Outline" requires a brief statement of the key point (1 mark) plus some development or context (1 mark)

> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked to "outline" a benefit, make sure you do two things: state the benefit clearly, then develop it by linking it back to the business in the extract. Many students lose the second mark by not explaining how the benefit applies to Emirates specifically. For example, don't just say "communication is faster" — go on to explain why faster communication matters for Emirates' environmental tasks such as recycling or reducing pollution.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> BrightPath Couriers is a growing parcel delivery business based in Manchester. It employs 200 staff across its warehouse, driving and administration teams.
> 
> The company recently updated its health and safety procedures. However, the new guidelines were only communicated through a detailed email sent to all employees. Many warehouse workers, who do not have regular access to computers during their shifts, were unaware of the changes. As a result, several safety incidents occurred in the first week because staff continued to follow the old procedures.

Which **one** of the following is a problem that can result from poor communication in a business?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is C**

Employees making mistakes because they have not received important information is a direct problem resulting from poor communication, as the intended message has failed to reach the audience, leading to errors in the workplace.

**A** is incorrect as increased motivation among staff is a benefit of effective communication, not a problem of poor communication

**B** is incorrect as faster decision-making by managers is an outcome of good communication, not a consequence of poor communication

**D** is incorrect as improved customer satisfaction is a positive result of effective communication, not a problem caused by poor communication

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Employees making mistakes due to not receiving important information

parts.problem_md: Explain **one **impact on a business of ineffective communication.
parts.solution_md:
Ineffective communication could lead to employees making mistakes because they have not received clear instructions **[1 mark] **which may result in faulty products or poor customer service **[1 mark]** leading to customer complaints, a damaged reputation and a potential loss of sales **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying an impact on a business of ineffective communication
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the impact, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - If communication between departments is ineffective, important decisions could be delayed **[1 mark]** because managers may not have the information they need to act quickly **[1 mark]** which could cause the business to miss opportunities or respond too slowly to changes in the market **[1 mark]**
> - Ineffective communication can lead to misunderstandings between employees and management **[1 mark]** which could lower staff morale and make workers feel undervalued or confused about their role **[1 mark] **resulting in lower productivity and higher staff turnover, increasing recruitment and training costs for the business **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three impacts on a business of ineffective communication will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *NEXT *is a well-known clothing retailer that operates in 70 countries and employs over 43,000 employees. Since *NEXT *commenced trading it has introduced many other products to its range such as home interiors, flowers and a wedding list service.
> 
> In 1999 *NEXT *launched its own online shopping platform, enabling customers to purchase its products where ever they live. It continues to improve its customer service by introducing new initiatives such as next day delivery.
> 
> *NEXT *mainly uses its own factories for production. However, it does purchase some clothes such as ladies dresses from Turkish factories.

*NEXT *works hard to remain competitive with other retailers of similar products.

Analyse why *NEXT *would want to remove any communication barriers within its organisation.
parts.solution_md:
Removing communication barriers would help NEXT to coordinate effectively across its operations in 70 countries **[1 mark]**. If information flows clearly between its own factories and the Turkish factories that supply ladies dresses **[1 mark]**, NEXT can ensure that all products meet the same quality standards, helping the business to maintain its reputation and remain competitive with other retailers **[1 mark]**

Effective communication across the organisation would also help NEXT to improve its customer service **[1 mark]**. With over 43,000 employees involved in areas from production to next-day delivery **[1 mark]**, removing barriers ensures that all staff understand new initiatives and customer expectations, reducing errors and delays that could lead to dissatisfied customers choosing a competitor instead **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying reasons why NEXT would want to remove communication barriers
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to NEXT's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the reasons to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - NEXT has introduced many new products since it commenced trading, such as home interiors, flowers and a wedding list service**[1 mark]**. Clear communication between departments is needed to manage this wide product range effectively **[1 mark]**, and any barriers could lead to stock errors or delays that affect the online shopping platform and in-store availability **[1 mark]**
> - Communication barriers between NEXT and its Turkish factories could lead to misunderstandings about product specifications or delivery deadlines **[1 mark]**. If ladies dresses arrive late or are made incorrectly, NEXT may not have enough stock to sell **[1 mark]**, which would result in lost sales and could damage its ability to compete with similar retailers **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six reasons why NEXT would want to remove communication barriers with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md: Explain one benefit to a business of using email as a method of communication.
parts.solution_md:
Email allows a business to send the same message to many employees at once **[1 mark]** which saves time compared to communicating with each person individually **[1 mark]** and provides a written record that can be referred back to, reducing the chance of misunderstandings **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a benefit to a business of using email as a method of communication
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefit, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Email can be sent and received at any time of day **[1 mark]** meaning employees in different locations or time zones can read and respond when it suits them **[1 mark]** which makes it a flexible and efficient method of communication for businesses with staff in multiple locations **[1 mark]**
> - Email allows businesses to attach documents such as reports, images or spreadsheets **[1 mark]** which means detailed information can be shared quickly without the need for a face-to-face meeting **[1 mark] **saving both time and travel costs for the business **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three benefits to a business of using email as a method of communication will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md: Explain one way a barrier to communication could arise in a business.
parts.solution_md:
A barrier to communication could arise if a business uses too much technical language or jargon in its messages **[1 mark]** because some employees may not understand the terminology being used **[1 mark]** leading to confusion, mistakes and tasks being carried out incorrectly **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a way a barrier to communication could arise in a business
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the way, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - A barrier could arise if there are too many levels in the chain of command **[1 mark]** because messages may be changed or lost as they pass through each level **[1 mark]** meaning the final recipient may receive inaccurate information that leads to poor decision-making **[1 mark]**
> - A barrier could arise if a business relies on one method of communication, such as email, for all messages **[1 mark]** because some information may be better communicated face-to-face or by telephone **[1 mark] **and important messages could be missed or ignored in a busy inbox, leading to delays **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three ways a barrier to communication could arise in a business will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> TUI is a holiday business with over 100 years of experience. It flies its customers to over 180 destinations around the world. It has 1,600 travel agencies and 27 million customers. Holidays can be booked by visiting a travel agency or online.

Explain one benefit to TUI of using its website to communicate with customers.
parts.solution_md:
TUI's website allows 27 million customers to access information about holidays and make bookings at any time of day **[1 mark]**. This means customers do not have to visit one of TUI's 1,600 travel agencies in person **[1 mark]**, which is more convenient and allows TUI to serve a larger number of customers without increasing staffing costs **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a benefit to TUI of using its website to communicate with customers
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefit, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - The website allows TUI to update information about its 180 destinations instantly **[1 mark]**. This means changes to prices, availability or travel advice can be communicated to millions of customers at once **[1 mark]**, ensuring that customers always have accurate and up-to-date information when booking a holiday **[1 mark]**
> - TUI's website can be used to collect customer data such as booking preferences and travel history **[1 mark]**. This information can be used to send personalised offers to its 27 million customers **[1 mark]**, helping to build customer loyalty and encourage repeat bookings **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three benefits to TUI of using its website to communicate with customers will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Saha is a small business in Türkiye that opened in 2020 with 15 employees. It designs and manufactures robots which are used in hospitals, hotels and restaurants. Saha provides a seven-day-a-week customer service for all businesses buying its robots. Saha has ambitious growth plans and aims to become a multinational business within five years to manufacture robots in all continents of the world.

Analyse the importance of effective communication for Saha as it plans to expand internationally.
parts.solution_md:
As Saha expands into manufacturing on all continents, effective communication will be essential to ensure that robots are built to the same standard across every factory **[1 mark]**. Saha's robots are used in hospitals to move medical supplies and in hotels and restaurants to welcome customers and deliver food **[1 mark]**, so any miscommunication about product specifications could result in faulty robots that put the safety of patients or guests at risk **[1 mark]**

Saha currently has only 15 employees and provides a seven-day-a-week customer service **[1 mark]**. As the business grows internationally, clear communication between new teams in different countries and the original team in Türkiye **[1 mark]** will be vital to maintain this level of service, because if customer queries are lost or delayed due to communication barriers, businesses may stop buying Saha's robots and switch to competitors like NIO, Zoox or Vention **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying reasons why effective communication is important for Saha
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to Saha's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the reasons to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Effective communication is needed between Saha's design team and its manufacturing operations **[1 mark]**. As Saha develops new robots for home use including cleaning, shopping, security and entertainment **[1 mark]**, any miscommunication during the design process could lead to costly errors and delays in getting products to market **[1 mark]**
> - Expanding internationally means Saha's employees will be working across different time zones and languages **[1 mark]**. With only 15 employees currently based in Türkiye **[1 mark]**, the business will need to establish clear communication systems to avoid misunderstandings that could slow down production and damage relationships with hospital, hotel and restaurant clients **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six reasons why effective communication is important for Saha with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> IKEA is a well-known home furniture retailer with stores throughout the world. It was started in 1943 by Ingvar Kamprad. He wanted to produce furniture at a price that people could afford to buy. He developed flat packs to avoid damage during transport. A flat pack contained all the materials needed to self-assemble a table, a chair or a bed.
> 
> All IKEA stores are run as franchises.

Analyse the problems IKEA may face from ineffective communication with its franchisees.
parts.solution_md:
If communication with franchisees is ineffective, IKEA may not be able to ensure that all stores worldwide maintain the same standards of customer service and product display **[1 mark]**. Since all IKEA stores are run as franchises rather than managed directly by IKEA **[1 mark]**, unclear instructions or poor information sharing could lead to an inconsistent customer experience, which would damage the brand's reputation **[1 mark]**

Ineffective communication could also cause problems with IKEA's flat-pack product range **[1 mark]**. If franchisees do not receive accurate information about new products or changes to furniture designs since 1943 **[1 mark]**, they may order incorrect stock or fail to provide customers with the right assembly instructions, leading to complaints, returns and increased costs for the business **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying problems IKEA may face from ineffective communication with its franchisees
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the problems to IKEA's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the problems to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - IKEA's aim is to produce furniture at a price that people can afford **[1 mark]**. If pricing information is not communicated clearly to franchisees around the world **[1 mark]**, some stores may charge different prices, confusing customers and undermining IKEA's core promise of affordable furniture **[1 mark]**
> - Ineffective communication could mean franchisees are not informed about delivery schedules for flat-pack products **[1 mark]**. If stores throughout the world do not know when stock will arrive **[1 mark]**, they cannot plan effectively and may run out of popular items, leading to lost sales and dissatisfied customers who turn to competitors **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six problems IKEA may face from ineffective communication with its franchisees with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *The Better Toy Store (TBTS)* is a children’s toy shop. *TBTS *has three shops in Singapore. Two of the shops are located in busy shopping malls and the third is located at the Jewel Changi Airport. *TBTS *has a website for customers looking to buy toys online.
> 
> *TBTS *selects toys to sell that are excellent for play, value, design and quality. All *TBTS *toys are environmentally friendly.
> 
> *TBTS *lets customers sign up for a Very Important Person (VIP) membership on its website. The website gives VIP members special rates and exclusive offers.
> 
> *TBTS *sells dinosaur toys for 22.80 SGD. VIP members get a discount of 15%.

Evaluate the importance of good internal and external communication to *TBTS*. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solution_md:
Internal communication is the exchange of information between people within the same business. External communication is the exchange of information between a business and people or organisations outside of it **[K]**

Good internal communication is important so that staff across TBTS's three shops in Singapore are consistent in the way they operate **[K]**. Employees in the two shopping mall locations and the Jewel Changi Airport shop **[Ap]** need clear information about which toys to stock, pricing and the 15% VIP discount to avoid errors at the point of sale. Without this, customers could be charged incorrectly, leading to complaints and damage to TBTS's reputation for quality and value** [An]**

Good external communication is also vital for TBTS, particularly through its website **[K]**. The website is used to sell toys online and manage the VIP membership scheme that offers special rates and exclusive offers to members **[Ap]**. If this information is not communicated clearly, customers may not understand the benefits of becoming a VIP member, meaning TBTS misses the opportunity to build customer loyalty and increase repeat purchases **[An]**

Overall, external communication is likely to be more important to TBTS than internal communication** [E]**. TBTS is a small business with only three shops in Singapore **[Ap]**, so internal communication should be relatively straightforward to manage. However, its website reaches customers beyond the three physical locations, and the VIP membership scheme is a key tool for building long-term customer relationships. If external communication through the website is poor, TBTS could lose online sales and fail to grow its VIP membership base **[Ap]**, limiting revenue at a time when more customers are choosing to buy toys online rather than visiting shops **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Good internal communication ensures that all three shops select the same environmentally friendly toys that meet TBTS's standards for play, value, design and quality → if one shop stocks products that do not meet these standards → it could damage the reputation of the whole business
> - TBTS could use its website to communicate new product launches or promotions to VIP members → this keeps customers engaged and encourages them to visit the shops or buy online → increasing sales across all three locations and the website
> - Poor external communication with toy manufacturers could mean TBTS receives products that do not meet its environmental standards → selling toys that are not environmentally friendly would contradict its values → and could lead to customer complaints and a loss of trust in the brand
> - Staff at the Jewel Changi Airport shop may deal with international tourists who speak different languages → if internal training on how to communicate with these customers is poor → TBTS could miss sales opportunities from the large number of travellers passing through the airport

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Beacon is a small chain of three pharmacies based in Dublin, Ireland. The owner, Niamh, employs 18 staff across the three locations. Niamh has noticed that important messages about changes to medication regulations are sometimes not reaching all staff, leading to errors. She also receives frequent complaints from customers who say they were not informed when their prescriptions were ready for collection.

Niamh is considering two options to improve communication:

- Option 1: Improve internal communication by introducing a staff messaging app so that all 18 employees receive updates instantly.
- Option 2: Improve external communication by introducing an automated text message system to notify customers when their prescriptions are ready.

Justify which one of these two options Beacon should choose.
parts.solution_md:
Internal communication is the exchange of information between people within the same business. External communication is the exchange of information between a business and people or organisations outside of it** [K]**

A staff messaging app would ensure that all 18 employees across Beacon's three pharmacies in Dublin receive important updates at the same time** [K]**. This would help to prevent errors caused by staff not knowing about changes to medication regulations** [Ap]**, which is critical in a pharmacy where mistakes could put customers' health at risk** [An]**

> **[case-study]**
> Nomad is a tour company based in Marrakech, Morocco. The owner, Youssef, employs 12 tour guides who lead groups of tourists on day trips across the country. Youssef has recently expanded by offering tours in three new cities. He has found that guides in the new locations are not always following the planned itineraries, and some tourists have posted negative reviews online saying they did not receive booking confirmation emails before their trips.

Youssef is considering two options to address these communication problems:

- Option 1: Improve internal communication by holding weekly video calls with all 12 guides to ensure everyone follows the correct itineraries.
- Option 2: Improve external communication by upgrading the booking system to send automatic confirmation emails and trip details to customers.

Justify which one of these two options Nomad should choose.
parts.solution_md:
Internal communication is the exchange of information between people within the same business. External communication is the exchange of information between a business and people or organisations outside of it **[K]**

Weekly video calls would allow Youssef to communicate directly with all 12 guides across the different cities **[K]**. This would help ensure that guides in the three new locations follow the correct itineraries** [Ap]**, maintaining a consistent experience for tourists and reducing the risk of further negative online reviews **[An]**

However, weekly video calls may not be frequent enough to resolve day-to-day issues** [K]**. If a guide in one of the new cities has a question about an itinerary between calls** [Ap]**, they may make their own decision rather than waiting, which could lead to the same problem of tours not following the planned route** [An]**

Upgrading the booking system to send automatic confirmation emails would directly address the negative reviews from tourists who did not receive trip details before their tours** [K]**. Customers booking trips in Marrakech and the three new cities** [Ap]** would receive immediate confirmation, giving them confidence in Nomad and reducing the chance of negative reviews that could put off future customers** [An]**

The drawback is that an upgraded booking system does not fix the problem of guides not following itineraries** [K]**. Tourists who receive a confirmation email outlining their planned trip across Morocco** [Ap]** would be even more disappointed if the actual tour does not match what was promised, leading to worse reviews than before **[An]**

Nomad should choose Option 1 **[E]**. The guides not following itineraries in the three new cities is the root cause of the negative reviews** [Ap]**. If the tour experience itself is poor, sending professional confirmation emails will only highlight the gap between what customers expect and what they receive. By improving internal communication with his 12 guides** [Ap]** first, Youssef ensures the product is right before focusing on how it is presented to customers **[E]**
